Averroes, the Moorish philosopher Ibn Rushd from twelfth-century Al-Andalus, synthesized Aristotelian logic with Islamic theology through comprehensive commentaries defending Greek philosophy against charges of heresy. He argued for rational interpretation of scripture and proposed that philosophical and religious truth could coexist at different levels of understanding. Though persecuted late in life for threatening orthodoxy, his works translated to Latin profoundly influenced Christian Scholasticism in medieval European universities, making him central to how Christianity engaged Aristotle.
